score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on current GOV.UK/legislation/Planning Data readback, explicit distinction between permission, condition discharge, lawful commencement and enforcement status, and fail-closed handling of section 73/73B and deemed-discharge routes.

sources.label: GOV.UK Use of planning conditions
sources.fact: Conditions must satisfy planning tests; pre-commencement conditions require the statutory process and conditions may require later discharge before specified stages.

sources.label: TCPA 1990 commencement time-limit guidance
sources.fact: Section 91 normally requires development to begin within 3 years unless a different period is imposed; permission date alone does not prove lawful commencement.

sources.label: Pre-commencement condition controls
sources.fact: A pre-commencement condition can prevent lawful start until complied with; written applicant agreement is generally required subject to statutory exceptions.

sources.label: Deemed discharge procedure
sources.fact: Deemed discharge is procedural and only applies to eligible conditions after the prescribed application/notice process; it is not inferred from silence alone.

sources.label: Section 73 condition variation
sources.fact: A section 73 permission does not erase the original permission; continuing conditions must be read from the relevant decision notice and discharge history.

sources.label: GOV.UK Enforcement and post-permission matters
sources.fact: Updated 6 May 2026; breach of planning control and breach-of-condition enforcement require actual authority evidence and are not inferred from missing public data.

sources.label: Breach of condition notice
sources.fact: A section 187A breach-of-condition notice is a specific enforcement instrument requiring compliance with identified conditions; its existence must be evidenced.

sources.label: GOV.UK Consultation and pre-decision matters
sources.fact: Necessary statutory-consultee pre-commencement conditions still follow the statutory applicant-agreement/exception process and are not presumed discharged.

sources.label: Planning Data planning application condition dataset
sources.fact: 5,305 condition records; collector ran 26 July 2026; origin is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement, so coverage absence is not negative proof.

sources.label: Development Management Procedure Order 2015 deemed discharge
sources.fact: Articles 27-30 prescribe application, notice, timing and exemptions for deemed discharge; eligibility is condition-specific.

sources.label: Pre-commencement Conditions Regulations 2018
sources.fact: The 2018 Regulations implement exceptions/process around written agreement for pre-commencement conditions; they do not make every such condition automatically valid or discharged.

sources.label: 2026 planning application fees consultation
sources.fact: Current consultation discusses section 73 and section 73B routes; consultation proposals are tagged DRAFT/CONSULTATION and are not treated as enacted parcel rules.

examples.result: A permissioned candidate is not promoted merely because permission exists; outstanding pre-commencement or stage conditions can still block lawful progress.
Three-year commencement wording is read from the actual permission/condition context; no commencement date is invented from permission age.
A section 73 application/permission is not treated as cancellation of the original permission; both decision chains require exact reference binding.
Deemed discharge is not assumed from authority silence unless the statutory application and notice requirements are evidenced.
Planning Data condition coverage is explicitly non-authoritative/MHCLG-created at present; missing condition rows are not evidence of no conditions.
A breach-of-condition notice is not inferred from delay, stalled construction or an undischarged condition; an actual notice is required.
2026 section 73/73B fee consultation content remains consultation evidence and is not substituted for current enacted procedure.
No parcel promotion occurs without exact permission reference, current decision notice, condition schedule and verified discharge/commencement evidence.
